correctness.rationale: The normalized path has cosine eigenvectors |v_k(x)|²=c_k d_x cos²(πkx/M). On the first K eigenmodes, K consecutive time samples factor into an invertible spectral Vandermonde times diag(v_k(x)), giving ratio d_x^K∏_{k=1}^{K−1}cos²(πkx/M). K=2,3 reduce to elementary trigonometric monotonicity and finite small M. For K=4 the signed product reduces to P(u)=8u³−10u²+3u; its derivative and bound |P(u)|<1/3 on u≤3/4 plus first-neighbor P(cos²(π/M))>1/3 at M≥9 and exact M=3,…,8 classify every tie. Independently enumerated all predicted maximizing locations for every M≤100, K=2,3,4, PASS. Symbolic polynomial bounds and Vandermonde furnish all-length proof; finite data alone does not.
